name: HSR Sync Failure After Takeover
description: HANA System Replication sync state does not reach SOK after a planned or unplanned takeover. The secondary shows SFAIL or SYNCING for an extended period.
symptoms: SAPHanaSR show returns SFAIL on secondary
systemReplicationStatus shows ERROR on secondary site
Indexserver trace shows reconnection errors
nameserver trace shows registration timeout
investigation: Check SAPHanaSR show or SAPHanaSR-angi show for current sync state
Run hdbnsutil -sr_state on both sites
Verify network connectivity between primary and secondary
Check HANA trace files for replication errors
Verify that AUTOMATED_REGISTER and PREFER_SITE_TAKEOVER are set to true in CIB
root_cause: HSR replication link not re-established after takeover due to registration failure or network partition.
fixes: Re-register secondary site: hdbnsutil -sr_register --remoteHost=<primary>
Verify and fix network routes between sites
Check and adjust HANA global.ini replication parameters
If SAPHanaSR-angi: verify susChkSrv.py hook is active

name: Fencing Not Triggered During Node Failure
description: Pacemaker detects a node failure but STONITH/fencing is not executed, leaving the cluster in a split-brain vulnerable state.
symptoms: Corosync reports node lost but no STONITH action in logs
crm_mon shows node as UNCLEAN
Pacemaker logs show no fencing attempts
SBD watchdog not triggered
investigation: Check stonith-enabled property in CIB
Verify SBD devices are accessible from all nodes
Check /var/log/messages for SBD and corosync entries
Run sbd -d <device> list to verify SBD slot status
Check Azure fence agent configuration if using AFA
root_cause: STONITH is misconfigured, disabled, or the fencing device is unreachable.
fixes: Enable stonith: crm configure property stonith-enabled=true
Verify SBD device connectivity and repair if needed
Check Azure fence agent credentials and API access
Ensure stonith-action is set to reboot

name: ANF Volume Throttling During Backup
description: Azure NetApp Files volume hits throughput or IOPS limits during HANA backup, causing backup failures or extreme slowness.
symptoms: HANA backup log shows timeout errors
ANF metrics show throttling events
iostat shows high await times on NFS mounts
Backup duration exceeds SLA threshold
investigation: Check ANF volume performance tier and throughput limits
Review HANA backup configuration for parallelism
Check Azure Monitor metrics for ANF throttling events
Verify NFS mount options (rsize, wsize, hard, noresvport)
root_cause: ANF volume throughput or IOPS limits exceeded during peak backup I/O.
fixes: Upgrade ANF volume to higher performance tier (Ultra)
Reduce backup parallelism to stay within limits
Schedule backups during low-activity periods
Split backup across multiple ANF volumes

name: Enqueue Replication Server Failover Failure
description: ENSA2 enqueue replication server (ERS) does not take over the enqueue lock table after ASCS node failure, causing SAP application downtime.
symptoms: SAP application servers report enqueue connection lost
sapcontrol -function GetProcessList shows enq_replicator stopped
Pacemaker shows ERS resource in stopped state
Enqueue lock table lost after failover
investigation: Check ERS process status with sapcontrol
Verify ENSA1 vs ENSA2 configuration
Check Pacemaker resource constraints and colocation rules
Review /var/log/messages for resource agent errors
Verify enqueue replication profile parameters
root_cause: ERS resource agent failed to start or the replication profile is misconfigured.
fixes: Fix ERS resource agent configuration in CIB
Verify enqueue replication profile (enque/replication_port, etc.)
Restart ERS resource: crm resource restart <ers_resource>
Check and update SAP kernel patches for ENSA2 fixes

name: Network Isolation Causes Split Brain
description: Loss of network connectivity between cluster nodes without proper fencing leads to a potential split-brain scenario where both nodes think they are primary.
symptoms: Both nodes report SOK as primary in SAPHanaSR show
Corosync ring marked faulty
No STONITH action despite node communication loss
Application connects to wrong primary
investigation: Check corosync ring status on both nodes
Verify network redundancy (bonding, multiple rings)
Check iptables/firewall rules for blocked ports
Review Azure NSG rules for inter-node communication
Verify SBD or Azure fence agent can reach nodes via out-of-band path
root_cause: Network partition without functional fencing allows both nodes to assume primary role.
fixes: Restore network connectivity between nodes
Ensure fencing is properly configured and tested
Configure corosync with redundant rings
Add Azure internal load balancer health probe
Test fencing regularly with crm node fence <node>
